title: Traumatic arrest at a crash - withhold vs. work + go
objectives: Start/withhold per 4.11 + 8.17: DOA passenger (5 signs + factor of death) vs EMS-witnessed arrest in driver
TCA priorities: TQ, pelvic binder, airway + BVM 1:10 - compressions alone do little
Scene < 10 min; direct to UVMMC (Level 1), trauma alert + 'in arrest'
AEMT: IV/IO w/o pausing CPR, warmed NS 500-1000 mL, epi per 3.2A, SGA + capno
Bilateral needle decompression is paramedic: rendezvous en route, never wait on scene
resources: AED/monitor, BVM, OPA, suction, SGA, IV/IO, warmed NS, epi 0.1 mg/mL, TQ x2, pelvic binder, capno, metronome. Engine 1 (3 FF). Paramedic intercept available. UVMMC (Level 1) ~12 min
dispatch: UVM Rescue and Williston Engine 1, respond to Route 2A, St. George Rd near Industrial Ave, Williston, for a single car into a tree, 2 occupants, one not moving. Caller is a passing motorist. State Police en route. Time out 2310.

scene.location: Route 2A shoulder, dark, 25 F, dry. Sedan front-end into tree, heavy intrusion passenger side.
scene.setup: Manikin 1 (driver) on ground beside open driver door - motorist pulled him out. Manikin 2 (passenger) belted in passenger seat.
scene.moulage: Driver: open L thigh wound w/ pulsatile bleed (pump/squeeze bottle), unstable pelvis, R chest bruise, blood in mouth. Passenger: PASSENGER card + head tag (no gore needed).
scene.roles: Motorist; 3 FF/EMRs; Trooper arrives T+6; evaluator calls AED + pulse.

patient.name: Tyler Benoit
patient.on_arrival: On ground, gurgling, barely moving. Dark pool under L thigh. Weak carotid, no radial.

SAMPLE: Motorist: "He was moaning when I pulled him out, now he's quiet"
Car vs tree ~2300 at speed, no skid marks; unrestrained, airbag deployed
OPQRST: Pulse lost at T+3 in front of crew (EMS-witnessed)

primary: **Pulsatile bleed L thigh** -> TQ high and tight, first
Gurgling, blood -> suction, OPA, jaw thrust; no collar
RR 36 shallow; R chest bruised, crepitus, diminished BS
Weak carotid 148, no radial; pelvis unstable -> binder
Cut clothes, no other major bleed; cold ground -> blankets
Hemorrhagic + obstructive shock -> **arrest at T+3 (EMS-witnessed)**: work it + go
secondary: **Apneic, no pulses, no heart sounds, pupils fixed + deformed skull** -> DOA (8.17)
Scalp lac, blood in mouth; skull intact
R lateral bruise + crepitus; poor R rise w/ BVM
Unstable on one gentle squeeze -> bind, no rocking
vitals_note: Arrest stages are 2-min cycles from EMS contact. Pulse 0 = CPR. AED never advises a shock.

vitals.other: Carotid only. R BS diminished. Pulsatile thigh bleed
**No shock advised**; organized complexes ~120 on screen, no pulse (PEA)

vitals.trigger: TQ + binder + NS + BVM 1:10, en route ~T+8
vitals.other: No shock. Organized ~110 (PEA). R chest still poor rise

vitals.trigger: IF medic does bilat NDT at rendezvous (~T+12)
vitals.other: Rush of air R chest; better rise. Weak carotid + femoral pulse

vitals.trigger: IF scene > 10 min, no TQ by T+5, or waits for intercept

vitals.other: Pads stay on. Keep warm. MD after 1000 mL

flow.give: Motorist: "Help him, the other guy hasn't moved." Show **PASSENGER** card when checked. Stage **A** (driver).

branches.if: Crew starts CPR on the DOA passenger
branches.then: debrief 8.17: 5 signs + factor of death; driver unattended -> Stage **E**

expected: Passenger: 5 signs + factor of death -> withhold, leave in place (8.17/8.6)

expected.text: Driver = priority; roles assigned, CC = commander

flow.give: Pulsatile thigh bleed, gurgling airway. Pulse lost at T+3 regardless.

branches.then: prompt: "blood is pumping out of his leg!" - no TQ by T+5 -> Stage **E**

expected.text: TQ high and tight L thigh, time noted (4.4)

expected: Suction, OPA, jaw thrust, BVM w/ O2

flow.give: Stage **B**. Trooper (T+6): "A wreck like this - is there any point?"

branches.then: critical (evaluator discretion) - EMS-witnessed blunt arrest -> resuscitate + transport (4.11)

expected: CPR + AED; BVM 1 breath/10 compressions; no collar before ROSC (4.11)
Moving to ambulance by ~T+6; scene < 10 min

flow.give: Stage **C** in the ambulance. Intercept calls (option).

branches.if: Rendezvous en route; medic does bilat NDT
Medic: "We're 5 out - hold on scene for us"
branches.then: expect CC declines, sets rendezvous en route; if crew waits -> Stage **E**

expected: IV/IO w/o pausing CPR; warmed NS 500-1000 mL (4.11)

expected.text: Epi 1 mg (0.1 mg/mL) IV/IO ASAP, q other cycle (3.2A)
SGA + capno; CPR quality in moving unit (belts, smooth driving)

flow.give: Stage **D**, then **F** w/ fluids. Medic gives TXA (paramedic, 4.4/4.11).

branches.if: Bleeding resumes past the TQ en route
branches.then: expect tighten, 2nd TQ just proximal (4.4), new time noted

expected.text: ROSC recognized (capno jump + pulse); vent 10/min, EtCO2 35-45
NS 250 mL boluses to SBP >= 90; MD after 1000 mL (2.24A)

flow.give: UVMMC trauma bay. Trooper (radio): "What did you touch on the passenger?"

expected.text: Early trauma alert + 'in arrest/ROSC' to UVMMC

expected: Report: TQ time, binder, fluids, epi, arrest + ROSC times

expected.text: SIREN for both pts incl. DOA findings; crew check-in

critical: Resuscitation started on DOA passenger, delaying driver care (8.17)
Resuscitation withheld/stopped on EMS-witnessed blunt arrest (4.11)
Life-threatening thigh bleed not controlled before/with CPR (4.4)
No BVM ventilation / airway not suctioned (4.11)
Scene time > 10 min, or waits on scene for intercept (4.11)
Compressions paused > 10 s for IV/IO, airway or moving
Epi wrong concentration (1 mg/mL IV) or delayed in PEA (3.2A)
No trauma alert / 'in arrest' notification to UVMMC
differentials: Pulsatile femur bleed, unstable pelvis, flat neck veins
R chest bruise/crepitus, poor rise, better after NDT
Trachea midline; flat veins (hypovolemia hides JVD)
R chest + thigh findings explain it
debrief: Why withhold on the passenger but work the driver? Recite the signs + factors of death.
In TCA, what comes before compressions - and why does CPR alone do little?
What can an AEMT do for a tension pneumothorax in arrest? How did you get it done?
UVMMC is 12 min: why < 10 min on scene, and why not wait for the medic?
How do you document and hand off a DOA patient left at a crash?

crew_card.dispatch: Route 2A, St. George Rd near Industrial Ave, Williston. Single car into a tree, 2 occupants, one not moving. State Police en route.
crew_card.on_arrival: Dark roadside, 25 F. Sedan smashed into a tree, passenger side caved in. Young man on the ground by the driver door, gurgling; dark pool under his left leg. Passenger still belted in, not moving. Motorist waving you over.

actor_card.Motorist: Shaken. "I pulled him out, he was moaning. The other guy hasn't moved." Points to driver.
actor_card.Driver: Moans and gurgles at first; goes silent and limp at T+3.
actor_card.Trooper (T+6): "A wreck like this - is there any point?" Asks crew not to move debris or the passenger.
actor_card.Paramedic intercept: By radio: "We're 5 out - hold on scene for us." Meets the ambulance en route if asked.
actor_card.Evaluator: Pulse lost at T+3 regardless. AED never shocks. ROSC only with TQ + binder + BVM + scene < 10 min + medic NDT en route.

show_cards.title: PASSENGER
show_cards.body:
Belted in seat. Not breathing.
Neck, wrist, groin: nothing felt.
No heart sounds.
Pupils large, not reacting.
Skull visibly deformed.
show_cards.cue: When crew checks passenger: all 5 signs + factor of death (8.17)

show_cards.title: VEHICLE
show_cards.body:
Driver airbag deployed.
Steering wheel bent.
No skid marks.
Passenger door pushed in ~2 ft.

show_cards.title: AED / MONITOR
show_cards.caption: NO SHOCK ADVISED
show_cards.cue: Every analysis from T+3 (PEA, no pulse). Stage E: switch to flat line, still no shock

show_cards.title: CAPNOGRAPHY
show_cards.caption: EtCO2 12
show_cards.cue: CPR, Stage B (18 in Stage C, 6 in Stage E)

moulage_tags.text: Open wound, thigh bent, bright red blood spurting
Bruised; crackly under skin; quiet breath sounds R
moulage_tags.cue: Breath sounds return R once medic decompresses

learn_more.focus: withhold vs start, hemorrhage control and ventilation before compressions, short scene time, tension pneumothorax
